channel.title: Anand Kumar: blog
channel.description: Write-ups on free-space optics, satellite QKD and the simulation work behind them.

item.title: QSAFire, a satellite SNS-TF-QKD simulator built layer by layer
item.description: How I built QSAFire during my internship at DRDO's Scientific Analysis Group, and why every stage of the link budget is checked against an outside reference.

item.title: SateSim, a satellite link budget simulator with a dashboard
item.description: How SateSim turns an orbit and a ground station into SNR, BER, Doppler shift and elevation, with a dashboard, CSV export and a PDF report.

item.title: Simulating a decoy-state BB84 satellite constellation over India
item.description: How the simulator behind my Springer paper works, from Walker-Delta orbits to the key a station collects in a day, and what its numbers do and do not say.

item.title: VeriSure AI, asking plain questions of insurance policies
item.description: How a hackathon prototype turns uploaded policy documents into a question-answering tool that cites the clauses behind each answer.

item.title: VibeSense, finding the products and the vibe in a short video
item.description: How a hackathon backend finds clothing items in a reel, matches them to a product catalog and names the aesthetic of the look.

item.title: DeepSpeak, building a chatbot from a person's own words
item.description: A look at a CodeClash 2.0 hackathon project that turns messages, photos and voice notes into a conversational persona, and the questions it raises.

item.title: Classifying paddy stress from 48 hours of weather, and testing it on a place it has never seen
item.description: A BiLSTM-LSTM model for three-class paddy stress, built with physiology-based labels and tested by holding out an entire coastal location.

item.title: An SNS-TF-QKD link in OptiSystem, and the Python pipeline that reads its logs
item.description: How I built a physical-layer sending-or-not-sending twin-field QKD prototype in OptiSystem with MATLAB co-simulation, and the Python pipeline that turns its CSV logs into a key rate.

item.title: Quantum Networks Under the Lens, Part 5: Can geography create quantum advantage?
item.description: Two identical systems in different places will not perform the same. Can geography become a strategic resource for quantum communication?

item.title: Quantum Networks Under the Lens, Part 4: Can stability be more valuable than performance?
item.description: A slightly slower network that is easier to operate can be the better one. A trade-off from working on large-scale satellite QKD.

item.title: Quantum Networks Under the Lens, Part 3: Higher satellites or lower satellites?
item.description: Coverage and contact time favour high orbits, while path loss favours low ones. Which should a quantum network optimise for?

item.title: Quantum Networks Under the Lens, Part 2: Is the atmosphere more important than the satellite?
item.description: Could the location of a ground station matter more than improvements in the communication hardware? A question about atmosphere and quantum links.

item.title: Quantum Networks Under the Lens, Part 1: Do more satellites always mean more throughput?
item.description: Adding satellites improves coverage, but does the useful key material grow at the same rate? A question from my work on large satellite QKD networks.

item.title: Quantum Networks Under the Lens, Part 0: What does it take to build a global quantum network?
item.description: The opening of a short series of open questions from my work on satellite quantum communication, asked before any results.

item.title: The theory of QKD is moving faster than its tooling
item.description: Protocols and proofs are advancing quickly, but the tools to simulate, reproduce and extend them are still fragmented. A note on what is missing.
